intent.raw_query: Eastern Europe city hop Prague + Budapest, $1200, 8 days, September 2026

experiences.name: Prague Castle Complex Tour
experiences.description: Explore the largest ancient castle complex in the world, including St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and Golden Lane. Walk through centuries of Bohemian history and enjoy panoramic views over Prague's red-roofed skyline.

experiences.name: Budapest Thermal Bath Experience at Széchenyi
experiences.description: Soak in one of Europe's largest and most iconic thermal bath complexes, built in 1913 in stunning Neo-Baroque style. A deeply cultural Hungarian tradition that blends relaxation with architectural grandeur and local social life.

experiences.name: Danube River Evening Cruise
experiences.description: Sail along the Danube at dusk to witness Budapest's illuminated Parliament Building, Buda Castle, and Chain Bridge. A breathtaking way to absorb the city's architectural splendor and understand its historical divide between Buda and Pest.

experiences.name: Prague Old Town & Astronomical Clock Walking Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the medieval Old Town Square, witness the famous 15th-century Orloj Astronomical Clock chime, and explore the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) with its haunting synagogues and cemetery that tell the story of Prague's rich Jewish heritage.

experiences.name: Budapest Ruin Bar Crawl & Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Discover Budapest's legendary ruin bars born from abandoned Jewish Quarter buildings, starting at the iconic Szimpla Kert. Sample Hungarian street food including lángos (fried dough), kürtőskalács (chimney cake), and local craft beers while soaking in the city's vibrant alternative culture.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Eastern Europe (Prague + Budapest)
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Use this time to rest on the flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing, take the Airport Express Bus (Line AE) to Dejvická metro station, then metro Line A to Hradčanská stop — total cost ~60 CZK (~€2.50). Check in to your Hradčany district boutique stay. Once settled, take a leisurely stroll along Nerudova Street, a charming cobblestone lane lined with Baroque townhouses leading up toward Prague Castle. Admire the architecture and get your bearings in the neighborhood without paying any entrance fees.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to the iconic Prague Castle complex exterior and Hradčany Square (náměstí Hradčany) for a golden-hour view — completely free. Watch the sunset over the city from the castle ramparts. Head back down through Malá Strana (Lesser Town) for a short evening wander.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport.
meals.lunch: Pick up a fresh trdelník (chimney cake) or a quick sandwich from a bakery near Hradčanská metro for under 80 CZK (~€3.30).
meals.dinner: Lokal Ujevezd in Malá Strana — a beloved Czech pub offering affordable classics like svíčková (beef in cream sauce) or goulash with bread dumplings for around 150–200 CZK (~€6–8). Wash it down with a draft Pilsner Urquell.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light — focus on arrival, check-in, and gentle neighborhood orientation. Buy a 24-hour public transport pass (120 CZK) if you plan to use the metro/tram more than twice.

day_by_day.morning: Full Prague Castle Complex visit — buy a Circuit B ticket (250 CZK, ~€10.50) which covers St. Vitus Cathedral, Old Royal Palace, St. George's Basilica, and the Golden Lane. Arrive early (9:00) to beat the crowds. Spend 2.5–3 hours exploring at your own pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk downhill through Malá Strana to the famous Charles Bridge (Karlův most) — free to walk across. Browse the baroque statues and enjoy views over the Vltava River. Cross into Staré Město (Old Town) and explore the Old Town Square: see the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) strike the hour, admire the Týn Church exterior, and browse the market stalls. Visit the Old Town Hall Tower for panoramic views (250 CZK, ~€10.50).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) from the outside — the streets and synagogue exteriors are free to view. Head to Wenceslas Square for an evening stroll and people-watching.

meals.breakfast: Grab a fresh pastry and coffee at Café Savoy or a local pekárna (bakery) near your hotel for under 100 CZK (~€4).
meals.lunch: Lokál Dlouhááá in Old Town — order the daily lunch special (polední menu) for 130–160 CZK (~€5.50–6.50), which includes soup and a main course.
meals.dinner: Restaurace U Provaznice near Old Town — hearty Czech mains like roast pork knee or fried cheese for 150–200 CZK (~€6–8). Very popular with locals.

day_by_day.notes: Prague Castle is the cultural highlight of the trip — don't rush it. The Circuit B ticket offers the best value for first-time visitors. Wear comfortable shoes as the cobblestones can be tiring.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Vyšehrad Fortress — a lesser-known but stunning hilltop citadel with free entry to the grounds. Explore the Vyšehrad Cemetery (final resting place of Dvořák and Smetana), the Romanesque Rotunda of St. Martin, and enjoy sweeping views of the Vltava. Take tram No. 2 or 18 from Malá Strana or metro Line C to Vyšehrad stop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Vinohrady and Žižkov neighborhoods — two authentic, non-touristy districts. Visit the Žižkov Television Tower (climb fee ~180 CZK/~€7.50) for panoramic city views. Walk through Riegrovy Sady park and enjoy the relaxed local atmosphere. Browse the vintage shops and cafés along Mánesova Street.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Old Town for a self-guided evening walk: cross Charles Bridge at dusk (magical lighting), explore the narrow lanes of Malá Strana, and end at Letná Park for a night-time city panorama — all completely free.

meals.breakfast: Prepare a simple breakfast at your accommodation or visit a local potraviny (corner store) for yogurt, fruit, and bread — budget ~60 CZK (~€2.50).
meals.lunch: Grab a klobása (grilled sausage) and mustard from a street vendor at Vyšehrad or nearby for ~80 CZK (~€3.30).
meals.dinner: Café Pavlač in Žižkov — a cozy local spot with affordable Czech-international fusion dishes for 150–200 CZK (~€6–8). Great local beer selection.

day_by_day.notes: Vyšehrad is far less crowded than Prague Castle and equally impressive historically. September evenings can be cool — bring a light jacket for the Letná Park visit.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Prague National Museum (Národní muzeum) on Wenceslas Square — recently renovated, entry ~200 CZK (~€8.50). The natural history and Czech history collections are excellent. Alternatively, visit the Municipal House (Obecní dům) for its stunning Art Nouveau architecture — free to walk in and admire the lobby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a self-guided walk through Nové Město (New Town): visit the Dancing House (Tančící dům) exterior for free, stroll along the Vltava embankment, and stop at Palacký Square. Visit the Mucha Museum dedicated to Art Nouveau master Alfons Mucha (~240 CZK/~€10).
day_by_day.evening: Last evening in Prague — head to Letná Beer Garden (Letenský zámeček) for affordable draft beer with an incredible view of the city (~40–55 CZK per half-liter). A quintessential Prague experience. Pack your bags tonight for the morning train to Budapest.

meals.breakfast: Visit a local café near Wenceslas Square — coffee and croissant for ~90 CZK (~€3.75).
meals.lunch: Nase Maso butcher-restaurant in Old Town — famous for affordable, high-quality open-faced sandwiches (chlebíčky) and meat dishes for ~150 CZK (~€6.30).
meals.dinner: Pivnice Radegast in Old Town — a classic Czech beer hall with mains from 130–180 CZK (~€5.50–7.50). Try the beef goulash or roast duck.

day_by_day.notes: Book your Budapest train tonight if not already done. The RegioJet or České dráhy overnight or morning trains offer great budget options (from ~€15–25 booked in advance). The journey is approximately 7 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Morning train departure from Praha hlavní nádraží (Prague Main Station) to Budapest Keleti Station. The journey takes ~6.5–7 hours — enjoy the scenic Central European countryside. Bring snacks and a book. Arrive in Budapest around mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your Budapest accommodation (book a budget hostel or guesthouse in District VII — the Jewish Quarter — for ~€15–25/night). After settling in, explore the immediate neighborhood: stroll through the Great Market Hall (Nagycsarnok) on Fővám tér — free to enter, browse the stalls of paprika, Hungarian sausages, and folk crafts. Walk across Liberty Bridge (Szabadság híd) for great Danube views — free.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Budapest's famous ruin bar scene in District VII — start at Szimpla Kert, the original ruin bar, which is free to enter most evenings. Enjoy an affordable Hungarian craft beer (~800–1,200 HUF/~€2–3.50) in this eclectic, artistic setting.

meals.breakfast: Pack snacks for the train: buy bread, cheese, and fruit from a Prague supermarket the night before — ~100 CZK (~€4).
meals.lunch: Eat on the train — bring your own food or use the dining car for a simple meal (~600–900 HUF equivalent).
meals.dinner: Karavan Street Food in District VII — an outdoor street food court with Hungarian and international options from ~1,500–2,500 HUF (~€4–7). Casual, fun, and very popular with locals.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday arrival in Budapest means the city will be lively. The Great Market Hall closes at 15:00 on Saturdays, so head there promptly after check-in. Purchase a 24-hour BKK transport pass (1,650 HUF/~€4.50) for unlimited metro, tram, and bus use.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Buda Castle (Budavári Palota) — take the historic Castle Hill Funicular (Budavári Sikló) up for ~1,200 HUF (~€3.30 one way) or walk up for free via the stairs. Explore Matthias Church (Mátyás-templom) — entry ~2,500 HUF (~€7) — and the Fisherman's Bastion (Halászbástya) for some of the best panoramic views of the Danube, Parliament, and Pest — free entry in September mornings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd) on foot back to Pest — free and scenic. Visit the Hungarian Parliament Building (Országház) exterior and walk along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó). Head to Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) — free — and stroll through City Park (Városliget). See the Vajdahunyad Castle exterior in the park — free.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Jewish Quarter more deeply: visit the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street (Dohány utcai zsinagóga) — entry ~4,500 HUF (~€12.50), the largest synagogue in Europe. Afterward, wander the atmospheric Kazinczy Street ruin bar area for evening drinks.

meals.breakfast: Molnár's Kürtőskalács near Váci Street — fresh chimney cakes for ~600 HUF (~€1.70). Grab a coffee from a local cukrászda (pastry shop).
meals.lunch: Buja Disznó in District VII — a beloved local lunch spot serving traditional Hungarian dishes like pörkölt (stew) and főzelék (vegetable stew) for ~1,500–2,000 HUF (~€4–5.50).
meals.dinner: Kőleves Kert (Stone Soup Garden) in District VII — a ruin bar-style restaurant with affordable Hungarian and international dishes from ~2,000–3,000 HUF (~€5.50–8.50). Great atmosphere.

day_by_day.notes: Fisherman's Bastion charges an entry fee after 9:00 AM in peak season — arrive before 9:00 to enter free, or budget the ~1,500 HUF (~€4) fee. Wear comfortable shoes for the Castle Hill cobblestones.

day_by_day.morning: Experience a traditional Hungarian thermal bath — visit Széchenyi Thermal Bath (Széchenyi gyógyfürdő) in City Park, one of the largest and most iconic in Europe. Monday mornings are less crowded. Entry ~7,500–8,500 HUF (~€20–23) including a locker. Spend 2–3 hours soaking in the outdoor and indoor pools.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Hungarian National Museum (Magyar Nemzeti Múzeum) — entry ~2,200 HUF (~€6) — for a deep dive into Hungarian history from ancient times through the 20th century. Afterward, explore the inner city: walk along Váci Street (pedestrian shopping street) and browse Vörösmarty Square.
day_by_day.evening: Take a free self-guided walk along both banks of the Danube at dusk — the UNESCO-listed panorama of the illuminated Parliament, Chain Bridge, and Buda Castle is breathtaking and completely free. This is one of Europe's most spectacular nighttime views.

meals.breakfast: Pick up fresh lángos (deep-fried flatbread with sour cream and cheese) from a street vendor near the thermal baths — ~600–900 HUF (~€1.70–2.50). A Hungarian street food staple.
meals.lunch: Főzelékfaló Ételbár near the National Museum — a self-service Hungarian canteen specializing in főzelék (thick vegetable stews) for ~1,200–1,800 HUF (~€3.30–5). Extremely popular with office workers — very authentic.
meals.dinner: Frici Papa Kifőzdéje in District VII — a legendary, no-frills Hungarian home-cooking restaurant. Mains like chicken paprikash or stuffed peppers for ~1,800–2,500 HUF (~€5–7). Cash only, arrive early as it fills up.

day_by_day.notes: The Széchenyi Baths are a cultural experience as much as a wellness one — Hungarians of all ages come here daily. Bring a towel or rent one on-site (~700 HUF). The evening Danube walk is best done around 20:00–21:00 when the lights are fully on.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the iconic Hungarian Parliament Building (Országház) — book a guided tour in advance online (~6,000 HUF/~€16.50 for non-EU visitors). Tours run every 30 minutes and last about 45 minutes. The interior is jaw-dropping — gilded staircases, the Holy Crown of Hungary, and stunning Neo-Gothic architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final afternoon in Budapest — visit the Citadella fortress on Gellért Hill for panoramic views of the entire city (walk up for free — about 20 minutes). The Liberty Statue (Szabadság-szobor) at the top is iconic and entry is free. Descend to the Gellért Thermal Bath area and walk along the Danube one last time. Do any final souvenir shopping at the Great Market Hall if it's open.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Budapest before any departures. Reflect on 8 days of incredible Central European history, culture, and city-hopping.

meals.breakfast: Visit a local pékség (bakery) for a fresh kifli (crescent roll) with butter and a strong Hungarian espresso — ~500–700 HUF (~€1.40–2).
meals.lunch: Hummus Bar on Október 6 Street — excellent value Middle Eastern-Hungarian fusion with generous portions of hummus, falafel, and salads for ~1,500–2,200 HUF (~€4–6). Very popular with locals.
meals.dinner: Menza Restaurant in District VI — a stylish retro-Hungarian bistro with excellent quality-to-price ratio. Mains from ~2,800–4,000 HUF (~€7.70–11). Splurge slightly on your last night — try the Hungarian beef goulash or duck leg confit.

day_by_day.notes: Parliament tours must be booked online in advance at the official website (jegymester.hu). If departing by overnight train or early flight, pack the night before. Budapest Keleti Station connects to Vienna, Krakow, and beyond for onward travel. Total estimated daily budget (excluding accommodation): Prague days ~€25–35/day; Budapest days ~€30–40/day.

trip_options.title: Classic Eastern Europe (Prague + Budapest) Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 – no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Hradčany district boutique hotel via airport express bus or taxi (approx. 30–45 min). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely first walk through Hradčany (Prague Castle Quarter). Stroll along Hradčanské náměstí (Castle Square), admire the exteriors of Prague Castle and St. Vitus Cathedral from outside, and wander the charming Nový Svět (New World) cobblestone lane – one of Prague's most picturesque hidden streets, just minutes from the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Head down to Malá Strana (Lesser Town) via the castle steps for a relaxed first dinner. After dinner, take an atmospheric evening walk across Charles Bridge, which is magical at dusk with fewer crowds than midday.

meals.breakfast: N/A – arriving at 13:00
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite near the airport or on arrival – try a local bakery/café near the hotel for a light sandwich and coffee (budget ~€8–12)
meals.dinner: U Malé Velryby (The Little Whale) in Malá Strana – cozy Czech bistro with solid svíčková (beef sirloin) and local Pilsner Urquell on tap. Mid-range ~€18–25 per person

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light – jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Focus on soaking in the atmosphere of your immediate neighborhood rather than ticking off major sights. September weather in Prague is typically mild (16–22°C), ideal for walking.

day_by_day.morning: Full Prague Castle Complex visit (opens 9:00). Buy a combined ticket (Circuit B recommended, ~€14) covering St. Vitus Cathedral, Old Royal Palace, and the Basilica of St. George. Arrive early to beat the crowds. Spend 2.5–3 hours exploring the Gothic cathedral's interior, the Bohemian Crown Jewels vault, and panoramic views over the red rooftops of Prague.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through Golden Lane (Zlatá ulička) – tiny colorful medieval houses where Franz Kafka once worked – included in castle ticket. Descend via the Old Castle Steps to Malostranská metro station. Head to the Old Town (Staré Město): explore Old Town Square, watch the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) strike the hour, and visit the Church of Our Lady before Týn.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) at dusk – walk through its historic streets and admire the exterior of the Old Jewish Cemetery and synagogues. Dinner in Old Town.

meals.breakfast: Café Savoy in Malá Strana – elegant Neo-Renaissance café known for its fresh pastries, eggs, and coffee. ~€10–15
meals.lunch: Lokál Dlouhááá in Old Town – beloved local beer hall serving fresh unfiltered Pilsner Urquell and classic Czech dishes like goulash with bread dumplings. ~€12–16
meals.dinner: Eska in Holešovice (short tram ride) or Mincovna on Old Town Square – modern Czech cuisine with seasonal ingredients. ~€22–30 per person

day_by_day.notes: Buy Prague Castle tickets online in advance to skip queues. The castle area is very close to your Hradčany hotel – a 5-minute walk. Wear comfortable shoes; the cobblestones are uneven.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) properly – purchase a combined ticket (~€22) covering the Old Jewish Cemetery (one of Europe's oldest, with 12 layers of graves), the Old-New Synagogue, and the Pinkas Synagogue with its harrowing Holocaust memorial walls inscribed with 77,297 names.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the Vltava River to Vinohrady or Žižkov neighborhoods for a local, non-touristy Prague experience. Visit the iconic Žižkov Television Tower (with crawling baby sculptures by David Černý) and enjoy panoramic views of the city from the observation deck (~€10). Browse the residential streets and independent coffee shops of Vinohrady.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city center for a classical music concert – Prague is world-class for affordable chamber music. Many churches (e.g., St. Nicholas in Malá Strana or the Estates Theatre) offer evening concerts of Mozart, Dvořák, and Smetana for €15–25. Book tickets at the venue or online.

meals.breakfast: Můj šálek kávy (My Cup of Coffee) in Holešovice or a local café near the hotel – excellent specialty coffee and avocado toast. ~€8–12
meals.lunch: Naše Maso butcher shop in Old Town – legendary open-faced sandwiches (chlebíčky) and meat rolls eaten standing up. Very local, very affordable ~€6–10
meals.dinner: Kantýna in New Town – upscale butcher-restaurant hybrid with premium Czech beef and craft beer. ~€20–28 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Jewish Quarter is emotionally intense – allow time for reflection. The Pinkas Synagogue especially requires a calm, unhurried visit. Book the evening concert in the morning or the day before.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip or final Prague exploration: Visit Vyšehrad fortress (free entry to grounds) – Prague's second castle, perched above the Vltava with stunning city views, a Romanesque rotunda, and the national cemetery where Dvořák and Smetana are buried. Far fewer tourists than Prague Castle. Spend 1.5–2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel, pack up, and check out. Take the train from Praha hlavní nádraží (Prague Main Station) to Budapest Keleti – the scenic Railjet train takes approximately 6.5–7 hours (book in advance via CD/ÖBB for ~€25–45). Depart around 13:00–14:00 and arrive Budapest by evening. Enjoy the countryside scenery through Bohemia and into Hungary.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive Budapest Keleti station (~19:30–20:30). Transfer to Budapest accommodation. Take a short evening walk along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) to get a first breathtaking view of the illuminated Buda Castle and Chain Bridge – one of Europe's most dramatic city vistas.

meals.breakfast: Café Imperial or hotel breakfast near Hradčany – a proper Czech breakfast of cold cuts, cheese, eggs, and fresh bread. ~€10–14
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from a local deli/market (Manifesto Market or Nusle market) for the train journey – cheese, salami, local pastries. ~€8–10
meals.dinner: Borkonyhá (Wine Kitchen) in Budapest's V. district – Michelin-recommended Hungarian bistro with excellent goulash and local Tokaji wine. ~€25–35 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the Prague–Budapest train well in advance (at least 2–3 weeks) for best prices. The Railjet is comfortable with a dining car. Arrive at Praha hlavní nádraží at least 30 minutes early. Budapest accommodation should be pre-booked in the V. (Inner City) or VII. (Jewish Quarter) district for central access.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Buda Castle Hill – take the historic Funicular (Budavári Sikló, ~€4) from Clark Ádám Square up to Castle Hill. Visit Buda Castle (Hungarian National Gallery, free on Saturdays for permanent collection), walk through the medieval castle district streets, and visit Matthias Church with its stunning Zsolnay ceramic tile roof. Admire the Fisherman's Bastion for panoramic views over the Danube and Pest skyline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the iconic Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd) on foot to the Pest side. Walk up Andrássy Avenue – Budapest's grand Champs-Élysées-style boulevard, a UNESCO World Heritage site. Visit the Hungarian State Opera House exterior and, if available, join a guided interior tour (~€12). Explore the elegant Oktogon square and Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) with the Millennium Monument.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Széchenyi Thermal Bath for a classic Budapest experience – the grand Neo-Baroque outdoor pools are stunning at dusk. Entry ~€22–28. Afterwards, head to the Great Market Hall area or Gozsdu Udvar (Gozsdu Court) in the Jewish Quarter for dinner and evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: New York Café (splurge-worthy experience, ~€18–22) or Gerbeaud on Vörösmarty Square – Budapest's most iconic historic café with extraordinary pastries and coffee
meals.lunch: Borkonyha or a casual étterem (Hungarian restaurant) near Castle Hill – try lángos (deep-fried dough with sour cream and cheese) from a street vendor for ~€3–4
meals.dinner: Mazel Tov in the Jewish Quarter (Gozsdu Udvar) – stunning ruin-bar-style Israeli-Hungarian fusion restaurant with a beautiful courtyard. ~€20–28 per person

day_by_day.notes: September weekends at Széchenyi can be busy – arrive after 18:00 for a more relaxed experience. Bring a swimsuit and towel (or rent one at the baths for ~€3–5). The baths are a non-negotiable Budapest experience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Hungarian Parliament Building (Országház) – one of the world's most spectacular parliament buildings, best appreciated from the Danube embankment and on a guided interior tour (~€18 for non-EU visitors, book online). Tours run every 45 minutes and include the Hungarian Crown Jewels. Spend 1.5–2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Budapest's Great Synagogue (Dohány Street Synagogue) – the largest synagogue in Europe and second largest in the world (~€15 entry). Visit the attached Jewish Museum and the haunting Raoul Wallenberg Memorial Garden. Then wander the VII. district (Erzsébetváros/Jewish Quarter) – explore the famous ruin bars (romkocsmák) like Szimpla Kert even in daytime (they open from noon on Sundays with a farmers' market).
day_by_day.evening: Take a Danube River cruise at sunset – 1-hour illuminated evening cruises depart from Vigadó Square and offer unbeatable views of the Chain Bridge, Parliament, and Buda Castle all lit up. ~€15–20. Afterwards, dinner in the V. district.

meals.breakfast: Café Gerloczy near Ferenciek tere – charming Art Nouveau café with excellent Hungarian breakfast of eggs, fresh bread, and pastries. ~€10–14
meals.lunch: Szimpla Kert Sunday Farmers' Market (10:00–14:00) – grab fresh Hungarian langos, chimney cake (kürtőskalács), artisan cheeses, and local produce. ~€8–12
meals.dinner: Onyx Restaurant (splurge option, Michelin-starred, ~€60–80) OR Costes Downtown for a mid-range fine dining experience (~€35–50) – treat yourself to elevated Hungarian cuisine for a special evening

day_by_day.notes: Book Parliament and Danube cruise tickets online in advance, especially for Sunday when demand is high. Szimpla Kert's Sunday market is a beloved local tradition – arrive by 11:00 for the best selection. The evening cruise is most beautiful after 19:30 when all the monuments are illuminated.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Museum of Fine Arts (Szépművészeti Múzeum) at Heroes' Square – world-class collection of European masters including El Greco, Raphael, Rembrandt, and Monet. ~€14 entry. Spend 2–2.5 hours. Afterwards, stroll through City Park (Városliget) – Budapest's grand public park with the fairy-tale Vajdahunyad Castle (free exterior) reflected in its lake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take tram #2 along the Danube embankment – one of the most scenic urban tram rides in Europe – south to the Liberty Bridge (Szabadság híd). Cross the bridge to Gellért Hill and climb to the Citadella fortress and Liberty Statue for the best panoramic views of Budapest from above. The 20-minute uphill walk is rewarded with a 360° vista of the entire city.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the ruin bar scene in the VII. district – start at Szimpla Kert (the original ruin bar), then explore Instant, Fogas Ház, or Ellátó Kert. These unique Budapest institutions are housed in crumbling pre-war buildings repurposed into eclectic bars and cultural spaces. A quintessential Budapest experience.

meals.breakfast: Artizán Bakery near Andrássy Avenue – Budapest's best artisan bakery with exceptional sourdough, croissants, and coffee. ~€7–10
meals.lunch: Gundel Restaurant terrace (historic, iconic) for a lighter lunch set menu ~€25–30, or Bagolyvár next door (same ownership, more casual) ~€15–20 – both in City Park
meals.dinner: Street food and bar snacks in the ruin bar district – kürtőskalács, langos, or a casual gyros/falafel wrap from one of the many food stalls. ~€8–12, leaving budget for drinks

day_by_day.notes: The Gellért Hill climb is moderately strenuous – wear good shoes. The view at golden hour (around 18:30 in September) is spectacular. Ruin bars get lively from 21:00 onwards – this is a late evening activity. Pace yourself with the local Dreher beer or Pálinka (Hungarian fruit brandy).

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest – visit the Central Market Hall (Nagy Vásárcsarnok) for souvenir shopping and last-minute food finds: Hungarian paprika, Tokaji wine, Pick salami, Unicum liqueur, and embroidered textiles. Browse the upper gallery for folk art and lace. ~1.5 hours. Then enjoy a final coffee at a terrace café along the Danube embankment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time – if afternoon flight, transfer to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport (30–40 min by taxi or airport shuttle). If time allows before departure, revisit a favorite spot or explore the elegant Váci utca pedestrian shopping street for last-minute gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Budapest. Reflect on 8 days of extraordinary Central European history, architecture, thermal baths, and culture across two of Europe's most beautiful capitals.

meals.breakfast: Gerbeaud or a local pékség (bakery) near the accommodation – final Hungarian breakfast with fresh pastries, túrós táska (cottage cheese pastry), and coffee. ~€8–12
meals.lunch: Central Market Hall upper floor food stalls – try lángos one final time or a hearty Hungarian sausage plate. ~€8–12
meals.dinner: Airport meal or in-flight – budget accordingly (~€15–25 at airport)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for airport transfer and check-in at Budapest Ferenc Liszt Airport. The airport is approximately 20 km from the city center. Pre-book an airport taxi or use the 100E airport bus to Deák Ferenc tér for ~€4. Declare any food items (meats, cheeses) if flying internationally outside the EU.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Eastern Europe (Prague + Budapest) Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private airport transfer arranged via luxury chauffeur service directly to Hradčany district boutique hotel. Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your premium accommodations with views over the castle quarter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk through the Hradčany district starting from the hotel. Stroll along Hradčanské náměstí (Hradčany Square), admire the Archbishop's Palace and Schwarzenberg Palace exteriors. Walk to the Castle Ramparts for sweeping panoramic views over the red-rooftop cityscape of Prague — a perfect introduction to the city requiring minimal energy after travel.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Lokál Hradčany or Villa Richter (situated within the Prague Castle vineyards) — a romantic terrace setting with Czech wine and seasonal European cuisine. After dinner, take a short evening stroll along the illuminated Castle walls before retiring to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or airport meal
meals.lunch: Light welcome snack or room service at the hotel upon arrival
meals.dinner: Villa Richter — multi-course Czech and Central European tasting menu with Bohemian wine pairings; expect USD 80–120 per person

day_by_day.notes: Flight arrives 13:00 — nothing is scheduled before arrival. Pre-arrange private luxury transfer (Mercedes E-Class or Sprinter) from Václav Havel Airport. Confirm early check-in with the hotel in advance. Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Full Prague Castle Complex (Pražský hrad) private guided tour beginning at 9:00 AM. Explore St. Vitus Cathedral with its stunning Gothic spires and Alfons Mucha stained-glass windows, the Old Royal Palace, St. George's Basilica, and the Golden Lane. Book a VIP skip-the-line experience through a premium concierge service.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend through Malá Strana (Lesser Town) via the historic Castle Steps. Visit the Baroque masterpiece of St. Nicholas Church. Explore the charming cobblestone streets and hidden courtyards of Malá Strana. Cross the iconic Charles Bridge — arrive mid-afternoon to avoid peak crowds — and admire the 30 Baroque statues lining the bridge.
day_by_day.evening: Cocktail hour at Hemingway Bar in the Old Town, one of Central Europe's most celebrated cocktail bars. Followed by dinner at Field Restaurant (one Michelin star) in Staré Město — a refined Czech cuisine experience with creative tasting menus using local seasonal ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet hotel breakfast — freshly baked pastries, charcuterie, eggs to order, fresh-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Café Savoy in Malá Strana — a beautifully restored Neo-Renaissance café offering refined Czech classics like svíčková and open-faced sandwiches
meals.dinner: Field Restaurant — 5 or 7-course tasting menu with wine pairing; USD 120–160 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book Prague Castle private guide at least 2 weeks in advance. Field Restaurant requires reservations 4–6 weeks ahead. Wear comfortable walking shoes — this is a high-step day across cobblestones and castle staircases.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Lobkowicz Palace inside the Prague Castle complex — a privately owned palace museum housing original Beethoven and Mozart manuscripts, Bruegel paintings, and remarkable Bohemian history collections. Includes a personal audio guide narrated by the Lobkowicz family. Follow with a coffee tasting at the palace café terrace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private half-day cultural immersion: visit the Strahov Monastery Library — one of the most beautiful Baroque libraries in the world — and the Strahov Brewery for a premium craft beer tasting. Explore the monastery's Picture Gallery featuring Bohemian Baroque art. Afterward, visit the Loreto Shrine, a remarkable pilgrimage complex adjacent to Hradčany.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical concert at the Prague Castle or the Lobkowicz Palace concert hall — both regularly host intimate chamber music evenings. Dress code: smart casual to formal. Conclude with a nightcap at Augustine Bar inside the Augustine Hotel, set within a 13th-century monastery.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast with fresh Czech kolache pastries and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Strahov Monastery Brewery Restaurant — traditional Czech cuisine paired with monastery-brewed beers in a historic setting
meals.dinner: Pre-concert light dinner at Malostranská Beseda — refined Czech and international dishes in a beautifully restored cultural hall

day_by_day.notes: Book Lobkowicz Palace tickets online in advance. Check the Prague Castle Events calendar for evening concert schedules — book at least 2 weeks ahead. The Strahov Library interior may only be viewed from the doorway; photography is permitted.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Prague's Jewish Quarter (Josefov) with a private expert guide. Visit the Old Jewish Cemetery — one of the oldest in Europe — the Old-New Synagogue (the oldest active synagogue in Europe, dating to 1270), the Pinkas Synagogue with its haunting memorial to Holocaust victims, and the Spanish Synagogue with its stunning Moorish interior.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Old Town (Staré Město) at leisure. Watch the famous Astronomical Clock (Orloj) chime at the top of the hour on Old Town Square. Visit the Church of Our Lady before Týn. Browse the upscale boutiques and antique shops along Pařížská Street — Prague's luxury shopping boulevard featuring Hermès, Louis Vuitton, and local Czech designers.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Prague at La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise — a Michelin-starred restaurant offering an extraordinary 11-course journey through historical Czech cuisine. One of Prague's finest dining experiences. After dinner, evening stroll across the illuminated Charles Bridge for a final night view of Prague Castle.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full gourmet spread
meals.lunch: Kolkovna Celnice — upscale Czech brasserie near Old Town Square; excellent svíčková, duck confit, and Pilsner Urquell on tap
meals.dinner: La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise — 11-course historical tasting menu with wine pairing; USD 180–220 per person; reservations essential 6–8 weeks in advance

day_by_day.notes: Jewish Quarter tickets are bundled — purchase the combination ticket covering all synagogues. Photography is restricted inside certain synagogues out of respect. Pack out of Prague tomorrow — arrange luggage transfer or hotel storage for an early checkout.

day_by_day.morning: Luxury private transfer from Prague to Budapest by premium car service or first-class rail on the Railjet or EuroCity train (approximately 7 hours by train, or 5.5 hours by private car). Depart Prague around 8:00 AM. Enjoy the scenic Central European countryside. Alternatively, consider a 1-hour direct flight if time is prioritized.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Budapest early-to-mid afternoon. Check into your luxury Budapest accommodation (recommended: Four Seasons Hotel Gresham Palace on the Danube, or Aria Hotel Budapest). After settling in, take a first orientation walk along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) with stunning views of Buda Castle and the Chain Bridge.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner in Budapest at Costes Downtown — a Michelin-starred restaurant in the heart of the city offering contemporary Hungarian and European cuisine. After dinner, take an evening cruise on the Danube to see Budapest's UNESCO-listed panorama illuminated at night — one of the most spectacular urban night views in the world.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure or premium café near Prague train station
meals.lunch: Dining car on the train or a packed premium picnic arranged by the hotel; alternatively stop at a café in Brno if driving
meals.dinner: Costes Downtown Budapest — contemporary tasting menu with Hungarian wine pairing; USD 120–150 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book private transfer or first-class train tickets well in advance, especially for Saturday travel. The Danube evening cruise should be booked through a premium operator (e.g., Legenda or Silver Line) — opt for a private or small-group VIP cruise. Budapest accommodation should be confirmed before Prague departure.

day_by_day.morning: Buda Castle Hill exploration with a private guide. Visit the Royal Palace (Hungarian National Gallery), Matthias Church — a stunning Gothic-Baroque masterpiece with colorful Zsolnay tile roof — and the Fisherman's Bastion for extraordinary panoramic views over the Danube and Pest. Explore the medieval streets of Castle Hill at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the iconic Chain Bridge on foot to the Pest side. Visit the magnificent Hungarian Parliament Building — one of the largest parliament buildings in the world — on a premium guided tour. Explore the elegant Lipótváros (Leopold Town) district. Visit St. Stephen's Basilica and ascend the dome for rooftop views over Budapest.
day_by_day.evening: Thermal spa experience at Széchenyi Thermal Bath — book a private VIP cabin or evening session (the baths are especially atmospheric after dark). Followed by dinner at Onyx Restaurant (Michelin-starred) on Vörösmarty Square — a celebration of refined Hungarian haute cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full luxury spread
meals.lunch: Café Gerbeaud on Vörösmarty Square — Budapest's most iconic historic café and patisserie, established 1858; enjoy Hungarian cakes, strudel, and coffee
meals.dinner: Onyx Restaurant — elegant tasting menu featuring contemporary Hungarian flavors; USD 150–190 per person with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book Parliament guided tour in advance — English tours sell out quickly on weekends. Széchenyi VIP thermal experience should be reserved through the hotel concierge. Bring a swimsuit for the thermal baths. Onyx requires advance reservations.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street — the largest synagogue in Europe and the second largest in the world — with its remarkable Moorish Revival architecture, Holocaust memorial garden (the Weeping Willow), and Jewish Museum. Follow with a walk through the vibrant Jewish Quarter (VII District) and the famous Gozsdu Courtyard.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Great Market Hall (Nagycsarnok) — Budapest's magnificent 19th-century iron-and-glass market hall — for premium Hungarian artisan products, paprika, Tokaji wine, and handcrafted souvenirs. Afterward, take a private boat tour along the Danube for a unique water-level perspective of the city's grand architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a performance at the Hungarian State Opera House — one of the most beautiful opera houses in Europe, rivaling Vienna's. Book premium box or stalls seats for a world-class operatic or ballet performance. Pre-performance champagne dinner at the Opera House restaurant or nearby Borkonyha Winekitchen (Michelin-starred).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Stand25 Bistro in the Jewish Quarter — a beloved Budapest spot for elevated Hungarian comfort food; known for exceptional Hungarian classics with modern finesse
meals.dinner: Borkonyha Winekitchen — Michelin-starred Hungarian wine and food pairing restaurant; USD 100–140 per person; pre-opera early dinner seating recommended

day_by_day.notes: Check the Hungarian State Opera House performance schedule at opera.hu well in advance — September is prime season. Dress code for the Opera: smart formal. Great Synagogue is closed on Saturdays; Monday is ideal. Private Danube boat tours can be arranged through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest — visit the Museum of Fine Arts (Szépművészeti Múzeum) on Heroes' Square (Hősök tere), housing one of Central Europe's finest collections of European Old Masters. Stroll through the grand Andrássy Avenue — Budapest's Champs-Élysées, a UNESCO World Heritage boulevard — browsing its elegant architecture and upscale boutiques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely farewell lunch in Budapest. Final afternoon at leisure — optional visit to the House of Terror Museum (documenting Hungary's Nazi and Communist occupation) for a deeply moving historical experience, or a final relaxing thermal bath session at the elegant Gellért Thermal Bath. Check out and arrange private luxury transfer to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Budapest. Reflect on an extraordinary 8-day journey through two of Central Europe's most magnificent capitals.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — savor it slowly
meals.lunch: Páva Restaurant at Corinthia Hotel Budapest — refined Hungarian and international cuisine in a grand Belle Époque setting; ideal farewell lunch
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for airport transfer and check-in. Budapest airport is approximately 30–40 minutes from the city center. Arrange private chauffeur transfer through the hotel. Ensure all souvenirs, Tokaji wines, and paprika are properly packed (wine in checked luggage). Consider purchasing Hungarian Tokaji Aszú wine as a premium take-home gift.
